content.hook: Never ride hungry between towns again

slides.title: Food between towns: *plan the gaps*
slides.body: A simple way to never run low on a self-supported route.

slides.title: Find the *longest gap*
slides.body: Scan your route for the stretch without shops. That gap decides how much food you carry.

slides.title: Check *opening hours*
slides.body: Small-town shops often close on Sundays and at midday. Resupply before the quiet stretch.

slides.title: Carry a *buffer meal*
slides.body: Add one no-cook meal beyond the gap. Headwinds and detours happen.

slides.title: Split the route, *spot the shops*
slides.body: Shorter segments make gaps obvious. Then look up food stops nearby.

content.caption:
Bikepacking resupply planning: how to handle food between towns.

Running low on food is rarely about the big picture. It's about one long gap and a closed shop.

Quick checklist:
1. Find the longest stretch with no shops.
2. Check opening hours (Sundays and midday closures are common).
3. Carry one no-cook buffer meal beyond the gap.
4. Break the route into short segments so gaps are easy to see.

BikepackPilot splits your route into 50 km segments and helps you find food, water, bike repair and lodging nearby. But the checklist works with any map.
